findings: Fourteen concurrent independent repository instances patch the same file; all ten recent paths, appearance, stage, layout and export directory survive.
A separate JVM holds the actual OS file lock: a patch times out as a typed failure without changing bytes, and succeeds after the child releases its lock.
Cancelling a waiting patch completes promptly and releases its channel; a later patch acquires the writer.
An unusable preference file is retained with its exact bytes before replacement; its finding and backup path remain in the returned receipt.
A stale appearance host patches only appearance. Newer recent paths and layouts are retained, and those unrelated fields do not cause an endless resave loop.
Production StudioMain constructs the locked repository for appearance saves. Atomic file replacement remains JvmFileSystem.write; schema and existing corrupt-file handling remain unchanged.
limits: Open Recent menus and lifecycle recording are not implemented by this foundation.
Cross-process locking coordinates writers using the desktop repository; external tools that replace preferences without taking its lock are outside that protocol.
